summary:
We developed Dancing with the SARs, an interactive web platform built to visualize and analyze Earth surface changes using NISAR Level-2 GCOV L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data. Featuring interactive before-and-after comparison sliders and a local observation log, the site guides users through four distinct real-world case studies—in France, Columbia Glacier, Limpopo, and Ambae—illustrating wildfires, ice dynamics, flooding, and volcanic activity.

Natural disasters and rapid environmental shifts frequently occur under dense cloud cover, thick smoke, volcanic ash, or polar darkness, rendering traditional optical satellite imagery ineffective. By leveraging active L-band microwave radar, our platform demonstrates how NISAR penetrates atmospheric obstructions and tree canopies to detect structural, moisture, and surface backscatter changes regardless of weather or lighting conditions.

This project is important because it transforms complex, newly public NISAR radar datasets from NASA Earthdata and the Alaska Satellite Facility into an accessible, intuitive educational and analytical tool. It empowers students, researchers, and communities to interpret radar backscatter signatures and understand how continuous, all-weather orbital monitoring supports disaster response and climate science.
details:
Dancing with the SARs: Seeing Through the Storm — Turning Raw Orbital Radar into Actionable Earth Intelligence.

Dancing with the SARs is an interactive, globally accessible web platform that bridges the gap between raw L-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) telemetry and real-world environmental decision-making using newly public NASA/ISRO NISAR Level-2 GCOV datasets. Built with modern frontend web technologies (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript) and powered by geocoded polarimetric data from NASA Earthdata and the Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF), the platform enables users to dynamically inspect surface changes across four critical global events—wildfires in France, glacial dynamics at Columbia Glacier, flooding in Limpopo, and volcanic activity on Ambae—via interactive before-and-after comparison sliders and a browser-based field observation log.

While traditional optical Earth observation satellites are blinded by dense cloud cover, thick wildfire smoke, volcanic ash, and polar darkness, NISAR’s active L-band microwave radar penetrates atmospheric obstructions and forest canopies to capture structural, moisture, and surface backscatter shifts 24/7. However, raw SAR covariance matrices remain notoriously difficult for non-specialists to interpret. Dancing with the SARs solves this bottleneck by translating complex radar physics into an intuitive, zero-barrier visual interface that requires no specialized GIS software or heavy data downloads.

The project’s creativity lies in transforming intimidating orbital radar science into an engaging, tactile storytelling experience—combining interactive visual diagnostics with an integrated field observation log. By making all-weather orbital monitoring immediately understandable and globally accessible, our platform empowers students, educators, citizen scientists, and local emergency responders to interpret radar backscatter signatures, accelerating public literacy and rapid situational awareness in an era of escalating climate extremes.
